**Camera and LiDAR provide complementary evidence.** Cameras capture texture, color, and rich semantic cues; LiDAR measures geometric range at sampled directions. Fusion tries to combine those strengths, but only if measurements refer to the same place and time. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17270) [2](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d9/d0c/group__calib3d.html)

Early or feature fusion combines measurements or learned features before the final prediction. It can exploit complementary local evidence but is sensitive to alignment. Late fusion combines independently detected objects, making components modular while potentially discarding information that would have resolved an earlier ambiguity.

**Bird's-eye view provides a shared spatial workspace.** Features are represented over a ground-plane grid so objects from different cameras or times can be reasoned about together. Moving from image pixels into that space requires geometry, learned depth or attention, and appropriate transformations. BEVFormer is specifically a multi-camera temporal/spatial design; not every BEV model includes LiDAR.

A timestamp error can place a moving car's camera appearance beside its LiDAR points instead of on them. Incorrect extrinsics produce similar misalignment even for static objects. Evaluate timing offsets, calibration errors, missing sensors, weather, and range. Temporal fusion also needs ego-motion compensation. The representation makes spatial combination convenient; it does not automatically solve synchronization or make uncertain sensor evidence exact.

**Technical details and references.**

Early fusion combines sensor measurements/features before final detection; late fusion combines independently predicted objects; BEV fusion projects or attends sensor features into a common ground-plane representation. Camera images offer texture/semantics, while LiDAR supplies geometric range. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17270) [2](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d9/d0c/group__calib3d.html)

A BEV representation supports spatial and temporal reasoning, but needs accurate calibration, timestamps, ego-motion compensation, and uncertainty handling. BEVFormer itself is a multi-camera temporal/spatial attention design, not proof that every BEV model fuses LiDAR. Distinguish it from explicit camera–LiDAR fusion variants.

Test missing sensors, weather, occlusion, range, and timing errors. Late fusion offers modularity but may discard complementary low-level evidence; early/feature fusion can exploit it while becoming more sensitive to alignment and sensor-domain shifts.
